svg.aria-label: Two chemistries at pore scale. (a) Dilute water dissolves gypsum into Ca2+ and SO4 2- until it is saturated, so it leaves carrying about 17 mol per cubic metre. (b) In 0.5 M sodium carbonate brine the released Ca2+ precipitates as calcite in the same place, the water never saturates with gypsum and carries about 500 mol per cubic metre away as sulphate: same kinetics, 30 times the capacity.
svg.text: fast near the inlet, then the water is saturated and stops
(b) 0.5 M Na₂CO₃ brine: dissolve and re-precipitate
CaSO₄·2H₂O → Ca²⁺ + SO₄²⁻, then Ca²⁺ + CO₃²⁻ → CaCO₃
Ca²⁺ is removed as calcite in place, so the water never saturates
gypsum one m³ of water removes
